question: Huawei is privately held and files nothing with the SEC. What revenue and net profit attributable to the parent company did Huawei publish for the first half of 2026 (six months ended June 30, 2026), how much did it spend on R&D (and what share of revenue is that), and what net profit margin does that imply? Note which profit figure you use, because two different 'net profit' numbers circulate.
grading: Key points (all required): (1) revenue RMB 467.82 billion, +9.55% (about +9.6%); (2) net profit attributable to the parent about RMB 23.43 billion (accept 23.4-23.5), down about 36.8% - OR, if the answer instead uses the Bloomberg headline net profit of RMB 23.81 billion (-36%), it must label that as the consolidated/headline figure; (3) R&D spending RMB 121.38 billion = about 25.9% of revenue (25.94%), up 25.2%; (4) implied net margin about 5.0% on the attributable figure (accept 4.9%-5.1%; 5.1% if 23.81 is used); (5) states that the figures are company-published, not SEC-filed. Optional: operating profit about RMB 32.77 billion (about 7.0% of revenue, one Chinese source). Fail if H1 2025 or full-year figures are used, if US dollars replace RMB, if net profit and its growth rate come from different definitions, or if the answer says Huawei filed with the SEC.
answer: H1 2026 (Jan-Jun, published 31 Aug 2026): revenue RMB 467.82bn (+9.55%); net profit attributable to the parent about RMB 23.43bn (-36.8%) - Bloomberg's RMB 23.81bn (-36%) is the headline/consolidated net profit; R&D RMB 121.38bn (+25.2%) = 25.9% of revenue; implied net margin about 5.0% (23.43/467.82; 5.1% on 23.81). Operating profit was about RMB 32.77bn (about 7.0%). These are Huawei's own published figures, not an SEC filing [W13-E1 to W13-E4].

output.answer:
## Huawei H1 2026 (six months ended June 30, 2026)

Huawei published these figures on **August 31, 2026** in its 2026 semi-annual report, filed with the **Beijing Financial Assets Exchange** (and disclosed via the Shanghai Clearing House) to satisfy its onshore bond-disclosure obligations — not an SEC filing.

| Item | H1 2026 | H1 2025 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | RMB 467.819bn | 427.039bn | +9.55% |
| **Net profit attributable to parent** | **RMB 23.428bn** | 37.05bn* | **−36.8%** |
| Consolidated net profit (total) | RMB 23.809bn | ~37.2bn | −36.0% |
| R&D spending | RMB 121.382bn | 96.950bn | +25.2% |
| Operating profit | RMB 32.771bn | — | −26.8% |

## Which "net profit" to use

Two numbers circulate, and they differ by only ~RMB 380m:

- **RMB 23.428bn (23.43bn / 234.28亿)** — net profit **attributable to owners of the parent**. This is the headline Huawei figure and the one in the Chinese-language reports (归母净利润). This is the right figure for a "profit attributable to the parent" margin.
- **RMB 23.809bn (23.81bn / 238.09亿)** — **consolidated total net profit** (group net profit, *before* deducting minority interests). This is what **Reuters** and most English wires led with ("net profit fell 36% to 23.81 billion yuan"), so it's the source of the discrepancy. CAIXIN and the WSJ variant (23.43bn) used the parent figure.

The gap (~RMB 380m) is minority-interest profit in consolidated subsidiaries.

## R&D

- **RMB 121.382bn** in R&D, up **25.2%** YoY (an increase of ~RMB 24.4bn, the single largest absolute increase of any expense line).
- **R&D/revenue = 25.94%** (Huawei rounds to ~25.9%, often described as "just over a quarter"). Up from 22.6–22.7% a year earlier. To reconcile with revenue: 121.382 / 467.819 = 25.94%. ✔
- Huawei said the money went into AI, connectivity, smart devices and intelligent automotive solutions. Management noted results were "in line with forecasts," but kept the full-year outlook under review citing external uncertainty and higher input costs (notably memory chip prices).

## Implied net profit margins

- **Parent-attributable margin: 23.428 / 467.819 = 5.0%**
- **Consolidated net margin: 23.809 / 467.819 = 5.1%**

(Roughly comparable regardless of which figure you use, because the parent/minority split is small.)

For context, the **operating margin** was ~**7.01%**, down from 10.49% a year earlier — the clearest measure of the core-business squeeze, and higher than the net margin because of the heavy R&D load and a drop in "other income" (government grants/asset disposals: RMB 8.325bn, −34.5% YoY).

## Caveats worth flagging

- The semi-annual report is a **condensed bond-disclosure document** — it does not break out results by business segment, nor the composition of inventory. Segment detail comes only in the annual report.
- A few aggregators ran a headline claiming R&D of "¥2.9 trillion" — that is a **currency-conversion error** (the figure is RMB 121.4bn). Ignore it.
- Other relevant items: operating cash flow swung from +RMB 31.183bn to **−RMB 39.885bn**; inventory rose 42.3% to RMB 277.494bn (described as active stockpiling ahead of supply/memory-price risk); gross margin narrowed from 47.47% to 46.11%; asset-liability ratio rose to 58.31%.

Sources:
- https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/huawei-h1-profit-drop-quickens-36-rising-costs-rd-spending-2026-08-31
- https://news.bjd.com.cn/2026/08/31/11940426.shtml
- https://wallstreetcn.com/articles/3780724
- https://www.mycaijing.com/article/detail/579894
- https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-09-01/huawei-profit-plunges-as-rd-spending-hits-record-high-102480691.html
- https://www.wsj.com/business/earnings/huawei-profit-slumps-by-a-third-on-r-d-expenses-raw-material-costs-3533ebad
- https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3365852/huawei-eye-self-reliance-ploughs-25-revenue-rd-expense-profits

claims.claim: Revenue was RMB 467.819bn in H1 2026 versus RMB 427.039bn in H1 2025, up 9.55%.
claims.reason: BJD reports revenue of RMB 4,678.19 hundred-million yuan, prior-year RMB 4,270.39 hundred-million yuan, and growth of 9.55%; converting hundred-million yuan to billion yuan gives RMB 467.819bn and RMB 427.039bn.

claims.claim: Parent-attributable net profit was RMB 23.428bn, down 36.8% from RMB 37.05bn.
claims.reason: MyCaijing reports parent-attributable profit of RMB 234.28 hundred-million yuan and a 36.77% decline. Dividing 234.28 by (1−0.3677) gives about RMB 370.52 hundred-million yuan, or RMB 37.052bn, which rounds to RMB 37.05bn; 36.77% rounds to 36.8%.

claims.claim: Consolidated net profit was RMB 23.809bn, about RMB 37.2bn a year earlier, down about 36.0%; the RMB 0.381bn difference from parent-attributable profit is minority-interest profit.
claims.reason: BJD reports consolidated net profit of RMB 238.09 hundred-million yuan, down 35.99%, and separately reports parent-attributable profit of RMB 234.28 hundred-million yuan. 238.09/(1−0.3599) is about 371.96 hundred-million yuan (RMB 37.196bn), rounding to RMB 37.2bn; 238.09−234.28=3.81 hundred-million yuan (RMB 0.381bn). The stated accounting distinction is consistent with the source's separate consolidated and parent-attributable figures.

claims.claim: R&D spending was RMB 121.382bn, up 25.2% (about RMB 24.4bn), the largest absolute increase among expense lines.
claims.reason: MyCaijing reports R&D expense of RMB 1,213.82 hundred-million yuan, up 25.2%, with an increase of about RMB 244 hundred-million yuan and says this was the largest absolute increase among expenses. These convert to RMB 121.382bn and about RMB 24.4bn.

The source gives the displayed inputs 121.382 and 467.819 (in the same RMB-billion basis). Their quotient is about 0.2594636, or 25.94636%; to two decimal places this rounds to 25.95%, not 25.94%. The source's stated 25.94% does not meet the requested half-last-digit tolerance for the stated inputs.
